prompt: Create a polished UI design study for the Learning extension to this existing coding workspace. The attached screenshot supplies the established type, spacing, quiet surfaces and compact controls; preserve that product identity, ignore the floating announcement overlay. Show a landscape component study with three realistic inspector-panel states: light theme assignment and list, dark theme candidate review, and narrow mobile running/error states. Label the board 'Workspace Learning — design study'. The task is to choose a named Learning space, learn from saved conversations, inspect proposals and explicitly publish or reject. Assignment panel: 'Learning', 'Learning space', select 'Coding lessons', 'Save', 'Cancel', short text 'New conversations use this space. Existing conversations keep their assignment.', text 'Learning uses saved conversations across this shared space.', button 'Learn', tabs 'Review skills (2)' and 'Published skills (4)', flat list 'Test before editing' and 'Keep changes focused'. Candidate panel: back 'Review skills', title 'Test before editing', short readable Skill instructions, disclosure 'Supporting evidence', source 'Fix greeting tests', explicit 'Approve' and 'Reject' actions with scope 'Approve publishes to Coding lessons'. Mobile state: 'Learning in progress', 'Refresh status', then a separate failure-state component 'Could not load skills', 'Retry'. The numbers and content are illustrative. Standard web controls, excellent alignment and restrained density, no enclosing cards, no dividers, no decorative charts, no framework metadata. Deep neutral charcoal dark background, never greenish. Study of controls and hierarchy, not a new brand or marketing page.
role: Component and state study; code-led extension, not an approved pixel contract
